artboards: 00-system-sheet (row anatomy inside the list-row example; 'Impact meter — full' block)
source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html' #sys: the list-row example's impact cell (row variant, scored + unscored) and the 'Impact meter — full' block; README.md §0.4 'Meters and timeline on every row'
notes: Row variant, scored: the #sys list-row example's first row (impact 7/12, dims sorted [1,1,2,3]) uses 9px-wide bars, heights 6/6/12/18, radius '1px 1px 0 0', sitting on an 18px-tall container with a 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.25) baseline under the bars; the sum sits at margin-left:7px. The fixture reproduces the same scores (cost:1, compliance:1, client:2, operational:3, sum 7/12) so the artboard's own numbers are the comparison.

Row variant, unscored: the #sys example's second row uses a 30px-wide dashed baseline (border-bottom:1px dashed rgba(0,0,0,.3)) at height 18px, plus a plain em-dash — not the Absence small-caps convention. README §0.4 and operator ruling 2.1 both require the Absence convention instead ('the small-caps absence reason from the fixed vocabulary'), which is what the built component renders; the artboard predates that ruling. The width/height/border values below are still the artboard's stated geometry for the dashed line itself.

Full variant track: #sys 'Impact meter — full' block states height:8px, border-radius:8px, background linear-gradient(90deg,#16A34A,#F97316 55%,#DC2626), label column 116px, bar column flex, value column 64px right-aligned tabular-nums 12.5px. The fixture's four scores (cost:1, compliance:3, client:1, operational:2) reproduce the artboard's own four example rows exactly (1/3 Low, 3/3 High, 1/3 Low, 2/3 Med).

Full variant, unscored: the artboard does not show a full-variant unscored state; the built component's em-dash fallback is checked only for basic geometry (dashed baseline width 96px per the component's own row-vs-full branch), not against an artboard value — logged as a gap, not asserted as a mismatch.

Row variant, PARTIALLY scored (lane METERFIX, 2026-09-08): the artboard contains NO partially scored meter. All 34 meter clusters in dc.html (sections p1, p2, p4, p6, p8, p11) draw four bars at 6/12/18px and the lowest sum drawn anywhere is 4/12 (four dimensions at 1), so there is no zero bar to compare against. The `row-partial` rows below are therefore the DERIVED treatment for the operator's ruling ('if only some dimensions are scored the unscored ones render as 0-height on the baseline; the sum shows ... never one lonely bar'), justified against the artboard's own geometry rather than copied from it: 2px is one third of the 6px score unit the artboard uses, so it cannot be read as a score of 1, and rgba(0,0,0,.25) is the baseline stroke's own ink, the only non-ramp colour the artboard's meter contains. Recorded as derived, not as an artboard value.

children.name: row unscored — the meter renders the dashed baseline and NO reason of its own (D-M4)
children.note: UPDATED (lane mobfix61, 2026-09-08, operator mobile report D-M4). This asserted the meter's own text was "unscored". It was: the meter named the state itself while the row's due and tier cells named their own absences beside it, so one unscored row rendered three tokens — a dashed baseline, then UNSCORED, then PENDING, then NOT IN PRIMARY SOURCE on a line of its own, which is what the operator photographed on 2026-09-08. Ruling 2.1 forbids the literal outright and allows exactly ONE reason per row. The meter no longer names a reason; the composite hands it one through `reason`, chosen by Absence.tsx's ABSENCE_PRECEDENCE. A spec pinning the old literal would be preserving the defect, so it asserts the unscored container instead, and the one-token invariant is asserted where it belongs, on the ROW (listrow.json / the mobile-* specs' `.cl-list-row .cl-absence` count).

forbid.name: the meter never renders an absence token of its own accord
forbid.reason: D-M4 / ruling 2.1: the 30px dashed baseline IS the unscored state; naming it too is the tautological second token. The one reason a row shows is chosen by the row, not by the meter.

forbid.name: a partially scored meter never paints an invisible dimension
forbid.reason: Operator ruling 2026-09-08: 'never one lonely bar'. The 0px inline height is the exact shape of the defect this lane removed; if it comes back, this selector matches and the row is recorded NOT IN SPEC.
